extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners, in-house communications teams, and agencies preparing entries for the PRSA Anvil Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation standards for preparing and submitting entries to the PRSA Anvil Awards, including eligibility, required materials, category definitions, and judging criteria for Silver (strategic), Silver organizational, and Bronze (tactical) awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility timeframe for entries
rubrics_metrics.description: At least some part of the work must have occurred during the period Feb 1, 2021 – Feb 1, 2023, though the program must have been initiated no earlier than Jan 1, 2021.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants should ensure the work submitted contains activity within the required dates; otherwise the entry is ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category applicability and multiple submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: An entry may be submitted in multiple categories, provided it applies to the specific criteria stated within each category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants should examine program objectives and target audiences to choose appropriate categories. Judges will not move entries to better-suited categories; use the 'Copy Submission' link to submit same entry in multiple categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges' award selection per category
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges will select only one Anvil, and up to two runners-up in each category/subcategory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If judges determine there is no winner (entries do not merit award) in a category, there will be no runner-up awards given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finalist and winner notification timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalists in each category will be notified by the end of March and posted online; winners announced in June at the Anvil Awards Ceremony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these dates for planning submissions and publicity timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic entry information required
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants must select category, provide unique title, organization/client name, agency name (if any), and a 100-word description of the program/submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each title must be unique or it will be renamed by organizers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Images upload limits and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload up to three graphic images representative of your program; images may be featured onscreen during the ceremony and in PRSA publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable file formats: jpg, tif, eps, native Illustrator, Photoshop or hi-res pdf files. Artwork should generally be at least 1,000 pixels in width or height.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit in English. Entries produced in a language other than English must be translated prior to submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All narrative materials should be in English to be judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics compliance and optional ethics commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: By entering, all entrants confirm their programs and entries comply with the PRSA Code of Ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an entry has an aspect of 'ethics performance' that is instructive and vital, include commentary of no more than four sentences. PRSA may take action if submission may not comply with the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: All entries must be submitted online
rubrics_metrics.description: All entries and entry materials must be submitted online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the online submission system; contacting awards@prsa.org is available for help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-page summary requirement for Silver Strategic Campaign
rubrics_metrics.description: The two-page summary (PDF) is the single-most important component of a Silver Anvil Strategic Campaign entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary should begin with a brief situation analysis and then address each of the four entry criteria — insights and analysis, planning, execution and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver supporting materials upload requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants must upload four separate PDFs (no more than 225 pages each with a maximum file size of 10MB) of any detailed supporting materials referenced in the two-page summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of relevant and meaningful supporting materials will result in significantly lower scores and may effectively eliminate the entry from consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: File format, page size, typeface and margin requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Uploaded documents must be PDFs. Pages no larger than 8.5 x 11 inches (A4 for international entries) with a minimum 10-point typeface and one-inch margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these formatting rules for all uploaded narrative/supporting PDFs to avoid technical issues with judging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver judging criteria — four core dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Anvil Judges will evaluate Silver Strategic Campaign entries on the merit of four criteria: insights and analysis, planning, execution and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your two-page summary and supporting materials should directly address these four areas; begin with a brief situation analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insights and Analysis (Silver) criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe methods/strategies/tools used to arrive at insights and analysis; indicate type of research — primary, secondary or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary research examples: focus groups, interviews, original data/analytics, surveys. Secondary research: databases, web research, industry reports, internal market analyses. Explain how insights informed strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning (Silver) criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the plan correlated to insights; provide general plan, specific measurable objectives, target audiences, overall strategy and budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives should be specific and measurable. Identify target audiences clearly and show how strategy flows from insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution (Silver) criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how the plan was executed and the outcome: activity flow, key tactics, difficulties encountered and handling, partner organizations, and use of nontraditional tactics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not entering under 'Integrated Communications,' advertising costs should not exceed one-third of the budget. Explain role of partners and any adjustments during execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation (Silver) criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe methods of evaluation, results, comparison to objectives, and how results reflect original strategy and planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide both qualitative and quantitative results and link outcomes back to the stated measurable objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-page summary and supporting materials linkage (Silver)
rubrics_metrics.description: The two-page summary must reference supporting materials; judges use both the summary and supporting materials to evaluate the four criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure supporting materials are relevant and clearly connected to claims in the two-page summary to avoid score reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-page summary requirement for Bronze Tactical Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise summary no longer than one page (PDF) is the single-most important component of a Bronze Anvil Tactical Award entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The one-page summary should include measurable objectives, target audiences, budget and category-specific information where requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze judging criteria — four key areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Anvil Judges evaluate Bronze Tactical entries on planning/content, creativity/quality, technical excellence and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media relations categories are NOT judged on technical excellence. Results should provide evidence (qualitative/quantitative) of meeting objectives and impact on broader programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze supporting materials guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants will be asked to upload supporting documents and backup materials as requested in each individual category (PDFs, videos, audio, links, URLs, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include all materials requested by the specific category to allow judges to assess planning, execution and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Relations (Bronze Earned) submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Tactics, programs and events driven entirely by media relations should submit press releases, media advisories, pitch letters, requests for coverage, etc., along with the one-page summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include measurable objectives and results, including media impact. Upload or provide YouTube/Vimeo links to any television or radio coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature Stories (Bronze Earned) eligibility and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature articles must be written by a practitioner and submitted/published through their efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the text of the feature article and documentation of publication/placement. One-page summary should include target audience, measurable objectives and documented results. Articles must be written in their entirety or substantively by the entrant, not merely pitched.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Communications (Bronze Earned) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Positioning of an executive across earned, owned, and shared platforms requires a one-page summary including info about the executive, stated objectives, and quantification of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include copies of significant placements, social media posts or internal memos to demonstrate impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Media (Bronze Shared) submission guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how social media was used to tell a story or connect with an audience; include screenshots or links and detailed results focusing on engagement and conversions where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For single-channel or multichannel entries, provide metrics and evidence of outcomes tied to objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paid Promotions (Bronze Paid) evaluation focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of sponsorships, paid placements, or other paid tactics that complement a broader PR strategy and generate exceptional ROI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate targeted, strategic use of paid tactics and show alignment with overall campaign goals and ROI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influencer Marketing (Bronze) submission expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Tactics focusing on paid spokespeople or key leaders to increase awareness and drive the brand's message; include achievements/benchmarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how the influencer met or exceeded campaign goals with metrics and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Platform (Bronze Owned) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If you launched or substantially enhanced a digital platform, explain how it was launched, risk involved, user value and how it matched goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include metrics and benchmarks. Entry can be completed by a vendor or the customer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Insights (Bronze Owned) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of data or research in a program to inform communications strategy and/or message development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how insights were acquired and specifically applied to strategy and tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Websites (Bronze Owned) submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a website as part of communications or content marketing should include screen grabs or copies of key pages and the website URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the site met or exceeded communications benchmarks and include evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Traditional Tactics (Bronze Owned) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovative, unconventional, creative tactics used as part of a PR program must be documented to show how the tactic specifically contributed to measurable results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload photographic and/or video representation of physical objects to be fully considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications entries (Annual reports, Newsletters, Magazines, Single-issue)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each publication category requires sample uploads and a one-page summary including goals and results. Newsletters and magazines usually require three consecutive issues; annual reports and single-issue publications require one sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear metrics or outcomes showing how the publication supported communications objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blogs/Vlogs and Podcasts submission guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Blogs/vlogs: provide rationale, target audiences, statistics and screen downloads plus the site URL. Podcasts: state purpose (teach/share), audience (internal/external), engagement across platforms, goals, results and listener feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include metrics, listener/download stats and examples of engagement or outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video and Branded Content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For videos, provide usage statistics or other quantified measurements to support objectives. Branded content: upload samples and one-page summary including goals and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly tie usage metrics to stated objectives and program outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Organizational Awards — Best In-House Team requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-page summary describing organization and outstanding accomplishments/strategic benchmarks; differentiate in-house role from external resources; include measurable impact, challenges, innovation and culture examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also upload two brief case studies (each 500 words or fewer). Provide number of employees on team and annual PR budget (including staffing costs). Current Silver submissions can be used as case studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Organizational Awards — Best Agency requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-page summary overview of the agency and accomplishments; include measurable client impact, challenges, innovation and culture examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload two brief case studies (each 500 words or fewer) or current Silver submissions; provide number of employees, annual revenue, and a one-page PDF client list from past 12 months including tenure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization with Most Impactful DEI Program requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-page summary describing team leading DEI efforts and detailing programs/practices/initiatives that brought positive DEI change; include future plans if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload two brief case studies (each 500 words or fewer). Submissions can include resources for diverse employees, internal programming and external impact examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best College/University Communications Program requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-page summary describing the institution and outstanding accomplishments in the last 12 months; include metrics related to admissions, graduation, first-year employment, internship placement and examples of academic achievements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other requirements: the college/university must have a PRSSA chapter and hold a Certificate in Education for Academic Programs in Public Relations (CEPR). Provide number of educators (full-time, part-time, adjunct) and faculty PRSA involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case study and word-count requirements for organizational categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Case Study Upload: two brief case studies or examples (each 500 words or fewer). Current Silver Anvil submissions can be included instead of case studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure case studies are concise, focused on measurable impact, and within word limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising cost limitation for non-Integrated entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless entering under 'Integrated Communications,' advertising costs should not exceed one-third of the budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If advertising is a significant portion of the program, consider entering under Integrated Communications or justify PR leadership in the campaign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category definitions as entry qualifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Each award category/subcategory includes a definition of the types of programs eligible (e.g., Community Relations = programs to improve relations in a specific geographic community; Content Marketing = strategic program creating/distributing valuable content; Crisis Communications = programs responding to unplanned events; etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants should read category definitions carefully to ensure program aligns with the category's intended scope and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media-specific submission items and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Many categories require submission of artifacts specific to the tactic (e.g., press releases, pitch letters, published articles, screen grabs of websites, video links, audio files, social posts, screenshots).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include originals or clear reproductions and links where requested so judges can verify placements and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurable objectives and evidence of results
rubrics_metrics.description: Across categories, entries must state measurable objectives and provide quantitative and/or qualitative evidence showing how objectives were met and how the entry impacted broader programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie metrics directly to objectives and include benchmarks or context to demonstrate significance of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entries become property of PRSA; judges' decisions final
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries become the property of PRSA. The decisions of the judges are final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By submitting, entrants acknowledge PRSA ownership of submission materials and accept judging outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of past winning case studies and educational resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants are encouraged to access the database of Anvil Award-winning case studies and view the 'Turning Your Triumphs into Trophies' presentation for guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use past Silver Anvil strategic case studies as benchmarks and follow tips from PRSA Honors and Awards Committee leaders to strengthen entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title uniqueness enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each title must be unique, or it will be renamed by PRSA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a distinctive title to avoid automatic renaming that could reduce clarity in jury materials or publicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image and multimedia inclusion for presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Images and multimedia uploaded may be featured at the awards ceremony and in PRSA publications for finalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select representative, high-quality visuals that communicate the program essence; follow file format and resolution guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-specific requested information
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual categories request additional specific information (e.g., budgets for 'Most Effective Campaign on a $5,000 to $10,000 Budget', three consecutive issues for newsletters/magazines, sample publication copy for annual reports/single-issue publications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the individual category instructions closely and include precisely the materials requested to avoid incompleteness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of authorship for published materials
rubrics_metrics.description: For feature stories and similar categories, entrants must document that the article/content was written in its entirety or substantively by the entrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide bylines, publication documentation, drafts, or editorial approval demonstrating the entrant's authorship role.
